chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Aslam, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Hashimi, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Aban ibn Abi Ayyash, from Sulaym ibn Qays al-Hilali, from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him)

He said: I asked him: 'What is the least that makes a man misguided?' He said: 'That he does not recognize the one whom Allah has commanded to obey, whose allegiance He has made obligatory, and whom He has made His proof on His earth and His witness over His creation.' I asked: 'Who are they, O Commander of the Faithful?' He said: 'They are those whom Allah has associated with Himself and His Prophet, saying: "O you who believe, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you."' I kissed his head and said: 'You have clarified for me, relieved me, and removed all doubt that was in my heart.'
ai.seo_question: What is the primary reason for a person being considered misguided according to Imam Ali (as)?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* from the chain of Sulaym ibn Qays, this hadith establishes that the root of misguidance is the failure to recognize the Imam as Allah's proof and witness over creation. It explicitly links this recognition to the Verse of Wilayah (4:59), framing obedience to the Ahl al-Bayt as an inseparable extension of obedience to Allah and the Prophet, thereby confirming their status as *Awliya al-Amr*.
